key_insight: UniGenDet unifies generative and discriminative models into a co-evolutionary loop so that a generator and a detector are trained together, exchanging adversarial signals to improve image realism and detection robustness simultaneously.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between independent development of image generation and generated-image detection—preventing detectors from lagging behind new generators and enabling generators to be evaluated/trained against realistic detection pressure.
method: Unified dual-path architecture: a generative network and a discriminative detection network share features and communicate via dedicated cross-task modules.

Co-evolutionary training loop: generator and detector are trained alternately with adversarial exchange (detector provides forensic feedback; generator adapts to evade detection), balanced by multi-objective losses for realism and detectability control.
Evaluation protocol: joint metrics and benchmarks that measure generation quality, detectability, and robustness under adaptive attacks to quantify trade-offs.
impact: Enables practitioners to build generative models that are evaluated against realistic detection pressure while producing detectors that stay effective as generators evolve—improving robustness in applications like deepfake mitigation and media forensics.

paper_title: UniGenDet: A Unified Generative-Discriminative Framework for Co-Evolutionary Image Generation and Generated Image Detection
paper_authors: Yanran Zhang, Wenzhao Zheng, Yifei Li, Bingyao Yu, Yu Zheng
